source.citation: H. Tran et al., Systematic study of Ge1-xSnx absorption coefficient and refractive index for the device applications of Si-based optoelectronics, J. Appl. Phys. 119, 103106 (2016).

data_lineage: Johs-Herzinger optical-model extraction of absorption coefficient

digitization.marker_center_method: Semi-automatic center localization from the black Sample A symbols using local-thickness/distance maxima, followed by visual verification on the 600-dpi render.
digitization.uncertainty_interpretation: Conservative NCMemSim digitization uncertainty estimate only; not a per-point experimental standard deviation reported by Tran et al.

selection.rule: Use the visibly steep Sample A near-edge branch beginning at approximately 0.7896 eV. Lower-energy detected markers are retained in the audit CSV but excluded because indirect absorption contaminates the low-energy region. The exact cutoff is an NCMemSim digitization decision, not a numerical threshold reported by the paper.
selection.upper_boundary_note: The highest selected marker digitizes to 1499.689 nm. This is 0.311 nm below the paper's nominal 1500 nm discussion boundary and is treated as a boundary-level digitization effect, not as evidence for a calibrated domain below 1500 nm.

split_policy.assignment: P01 validation, P02 fit, P03 validation, P04 fit, P05 validation, P06 fit, P07 validation, P08 fit
split_policy.warning: Fit and validation subsets are disjoint holdouts from the same published curve; they are not independent experiments.

limitations: The PDF does not provide a machine-readable alpha(lambda) table.
The digitized alpha values are not raw Psi/Delta ellipsometry data.
The plotted alpha points were themselves obtained through a Johs-Herzinger optical model.
No per-point experimental alpha uncertainty is reported in the figure.
Current NCMemSim optical dataset schema does not represent wavelength uncertainty.

The reported Sample A direct gap is 0.805 +/- 0.037 eV, whereas the current NCMemSim pure-Ge direct-gap endpoint is fixed separately; this difference must be treated as a model-assumption issue in F4f1.
